description:
It's Okay to Sleep In | Slow Santoor | 3 Hours of Permission to Rest

You do not have to earn tomorrow morning. If you go to bed with the alarm already set in your mind, this is three hours of quiet permission: nothing to get up for, nowhere to be, just rest that runs all night.

This soft Indian santoor music is designed to slow a busy mind at bedtime and keep the night unbroken - gentle, spacious and warm, never sudden.

Enjoy 3 hours of slow hammered santoor with long fading resonance, no drums, smooth transitions, no vocals and no sounds to wake you.

▶ Keep the night going — the full Sleep Music playlist:
https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=VIDEO_ID&list=PLeZN0byo199mx7da__pC4JseKqY856ABr
(paste this video's own id in place of VIDEO_ID before publishing — it opens the playlist at this video so the next one plays automatically)

Perfect for sleeping in, falling asleep faster, staying asleep, sleepless nights, light sleepers, weekend lie-ins, afternoon naps, bedtime reading, calming a busy mind at night, or quiet overnight background.

🎵 ABOUT THIS MUSIC
Instrument: Santoor (Indian hammered dulcimer), solo
Raga: Bageshri (a late-evening raga - tender, introspective)
Style: Indian classical ambient
Mood: Soft, unhurried, safe
Atmosphere: Curtains drawn, alarm off, the whole night ahead
Duration: 3 hours

🎧 HOW TO USE
Start it as you get into bed and set the volume just above silence. Let the long shimmer of each note carry you down. The music keeps going long after you fall asleep, so if you wake in the night it is still there to ease you back. Low speakers or soft sleep headphones both work.

⏱ CHAPTERS
0:00 Permission to rest
15:00 The alarm goes face-down
30:00 Shoulders let go
45:00 Slow shimmer
1:00:00 Drifting under
1:15:00 Deep and quiet
1:30:00 Nothing to get up for
1:45:00 Held through the night
2:00:00 Softer still
2:15:00 Unbroken rest
2:30:00 Dreamless quiet
2:45:00 Gentle light, no rush

⏱ BEST FOR
• Sleeping in without guilt
• Falling asleep faster
• Staying asleep through the night
• Sleepless or restless nights
• Light sleepers
• Weekend lie-ins and naps
• Bedtime reading
• Calming a busy mind at night
• Meditation before sleep
• Waking up rested
